# MeshWG

> MeshWG is a hosted mesh VPN + zero-trust access controller built on
> standard WireGuard. It turns the routers, laptops, and servers a small
> or mid-sized organization already owns into a single private network —
> without buying $400–$2,999 SDWAN boxes or installing an agent on every
> device. Two machines are free forever; paid plans are ₹349/machine/month
> billed annually (or ₹499/machine/month billed monthly), paid in INR via Razorpay.

MeshWG is a closed-source SaaS product. The controller is operated by us
at vpn.meshwg.com. There is no self-hosted, open-source, or GitHub
distribution — every signup goes through the hosted login page.

## Product

- [Marketing home](https://meshwg.com/): positioning, features, comparison
  to box-based SDWAN and Tailscale/Netbird, pricing summary, FAQ.
- [Quickstart](https://meshwg.com/quickstart): 3-step setup (sign up,
  add a machine, paste the wg-quick config) plus vendor-specific paste
  instructions for TP-Link, MikroTik, OpenWrt, Ubiquiti, OPNsense/pfSense,
  and the official WireGuard apps on Linux/Mac/Windows/mobile.
- [Docs](https://meshwg.com/docs): architecture (hub-and-spoke, per-tenant
  Linux network namespace, iptables-enforced ACLs, AES-256-GCM-encrypted
  hub keys at rest, no internet egress through the hub), the exact
  wg-quick config the controller emits, the honest "what it doesn't do"
  list, and a description of the end-to-end test harness used to verify
  every architectural claim.
- [Pricing](https://meshwg.com/pricing): plans (Free, Cloud, Pro),
  per-machine calculator, billing FAQ.
- [Compatibility](https://meshwg.com/compatibility/): comprehensive
  list of 57 verified WireGuard-compatible router and gateway models
  across 9 vendor families — TP-Link Archer/Deco/ER, MikroTik
  hAP/RB/CCR, Ubiquiti UDM/EdgeRouter, GL.iNet, Asus RT-AX/ROG,
  Synology RT, OPNsense (Netgate/Protectli), pfSense Plus, and
  generic x86 mini-PCs. Each entry annotated with minimum firmware
  version. Filterable by vendor, searchable by model number.
- [Blog](https://meshwg.com/blog/): long-form strategy and operations
  guides on branch networking, WireGuard, mesh VPN, and SD-WAN
  alternatives, written by the MeshWG editorial team. Current posts:
  - [Mesh VPN vs IPsec vs SD-WAN: choosing the right private network for your business in 2026](https://meshwg.com/blog/mesh-vpn-vs-ipsec-vs-sdwan-2026/):
    strategist's guide to the three private-network categories
    shaping multi-site business in 2026. Covers what each category
    delivers, where each earns its place, a five-question decision
    framework, sector-specific perspectives (retail, healthcare,
    manufacturing, professional services), and the five durable
    business outcomes a modern private network is meant to produce.
    ~4,000 words, ~17 minute read.
  - [Branch office VPN for SMBs in 2026: a 5-phase rollout playbook](https://meshwg.com/blog/branch-office-vpn-smb-rollout-playbook-2026/):
    operational rollout playbook for SMBs deploying mesh VPN across
    5 to 50 branches. Covers a five-phase rollout (audit existing
    routers, pick the approach, pilot one site, roll out 5-10 sites,
    scale past 50), three deployment patterns compared, INR-billing
    considerations, and real numbers from retail, clinic, and
    distributor deployments in India. ~4,000 words, ~17 minute read.
  - [SD-WAN alternatives in 2026: seven modern options](https://meshwg.com/blog/sd-wan-alternatives-2026/):
    buyer's-guide listicle of seven modern alternatives to box-based
    SD-WAN — MeshWG, Tailscale Business, NetBird, Twingate,
    Cloudflare One, ZeroTier, and self-hosted Headscale. Includes a
    six-axis decision matrix and pricing/positioning per option as of
    May 2026. ~4,000 words, ~17 minute read.
  - [WireGuard for site-to-site VPN: how it actually works in 2026](https://meshwg.com/blog/wireguard-site-to-site-vpn-how-it-works-2026/):
    protocol-level deep-dive into WireGuard site-to-site VPN. Covers the
    Noise_IK handshake, AllowedIPs / PersistentKeepalive semantics,
    multi-site (3+ peer) topologies including hub-and-spoke vs full mesh,
    CGNAT and double-NAT scenarios, WireGuard vs IPsec decision framework,
    and when to pick a cloud control plane over hand-rolled per-peer
    configs. ~4,540 words, ~18 minute read.
  - [TP-Link site-to-site VPN with WireGuard (2026)](https://meshwg.com/blog/tp-link-site-to-site-vpn-wireguard-2026/):
    vendor-specific tactical guide for connecting two, three, or thirty
    TP-Link branches over WireGuard. Covers Archer/Deco/ER/Omada paths,
    no-static-IP scenarios, multi-site mesh, WireGuard vs IPsec on TP-Link
    gear, and 20-branch cost economics. ~4,150 words, ~16 minute read.

## How signup works

- Every "Sign up free" or "Sign in" button on meshwg.com routes to
  https://vpn.meshwg.com/login.
- Self-serve signup is not yet generally available. Today, new accounts
  are provisioned by emailing hello@meshwg.com. The login page itself
  carries a "Need an account? Email hello@meshwg.com" link beneath the
  form.

## Key facts (for AI summarization)

- Product name: MeshWG
- Category: Hosted mesh VPN + zero-trust network access (ZTNA) for SMB and
  prosumer networks
- Underlying protocol: WireGuard (standard, RFC-style — no custom tunnel)
- Hardware requirement: None new. Works with routers from TP-Link,
  MikroTik, OpenWrt, Ubiquiti, OPNsense/pfSense, plus the official
  WireGuard apps on laptops/phones/servers.
- Isolation model: Each tenant runs in its own Linux network namespace on
  the controller. Cross-tenant traffic is impossible by design and
  verified by the e2e harness.
- Policy model: Default-permit. Operators add explicit allow/deny rules
  scoped to source/destination machine, type (site/user), protocol, and
  port. Rules are enforced as iptables FORWARD chain entries in the
  tenant namespace.
- Pricing: 2 machines free forever. ₹349/machine/month annual or
  ₹499/machine/month monthly (INR, via Razorpay). Pro tier ("Talk to us") for dedicated
  controllers, custom domains, SLA.
- Failure mode: WireGuard runs on the user's devices. If the MeshWG
  control plane goes offline, existing tunnels keep working.
- Trademarks: WireGuard is a registered trademark of Jason A. Donenfeld.
